# Task: accounts (branch demo/accounts). SHOULD/STRETCH feature: must not threaten the main demo. Owns studio/accounts/ (new), studio/web/js/account/ (new), studio/web/css/account.css (new). Do not edit studio/server/app.py or studio/web/index.html (owned by other agents): expose one hook `studio/accounts/install.py: install(app) -> None` that registers routers and startup, and a self-contained `studio/web/js/account/account.js` (ES module, injects its own DOM into the top bar at runtime). The integrator will add the two wiring lines. Allowed network: PyPI only. Reference code you MAY read (read-only): `webapp/backend/auth.py`, `db.py`, `models.py`, `routers/auth.py` from the earlier Streamlit webapp; do not copy its password/JWT flaws (it regenerated the JWT secret on every restart, which logged everyone out).

Objective: lightweight accounts + persistence so scientists can save runs and manual sessions and keep domain profiles. Guests keep full access to everything else.

Build
1. `db.py`: SQLAlchemy 2.0 + SQLite at env `STUDIO_DB_PATH` (default `$STUDIO_CACHE_DIR/studio.db`, else `./.cache/studio/studio.db`), WAL mode, created automatically on startup (no migration scripts). Tables: `users(id, username unique lowercase, pw_hash, created_at)`, `saved_runs(id, user_id, title, stage, target_id, seed_smiles, headline, events_json, created_at)`, `manual_sessions(id, user_id, seed_smiles, target_id, steps_json, created_at)`, `profiles(id, user_id, name, json, created_at)`. Parametrised queries only.
2. `auth.py`: signup/login with bcrypt (cost 12), username 3-32 chars `[a-z0-9_-]`, password >= 8 and <= 72 bytes, no email, no PII. JWT HS256 with secret from env `STUDIO_JWT_SECRET`; if unset, generate ONCE and persist to a 0600 file in the cache dir (never regenerate per restart). Session via an httpOnly cookie `studio_auth` (SameSite=Lax, `Secure` when `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`) and also accept a Bearer token. CSRF: every state-changing route requires header `X-Requested-With: studio`. Rate-limit signup/login per client IP and per cookie (in-memory), constant-time comparisons, uniform error messages (no username enumeration), never log passwords or tokens.
3. Routes (all under `/api`, JSON): `POST /auth/signup`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /me` (guest when not logged in), `GET/POST /library/runs` (POST validates `events` as a list of `studio.schema.Event`, <= 2 MB, owner = current user; GET lists summaries), `GET/DELETE /library/runs/{id}` (returns events for replay), `GET/POST /library/manual` (manual sessions saved from the manual export format), `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /profiles`. A profile JSON: `name`, `target_id?`, `objectives: dict[str, ObjectiveSpec]`, `avoid_smarts: list[str]` (each parsed with RDKit `MolFromSmarts`, <= 20 items, <= 200 chars each, reject invalid), `edit_allowlist: list[str]` (validated against `studio.registry.get_registry()` ids when importable). Strict cross-user isolation: a user can never read or modify another user's rows (return 404, not 403).
4. `profile_scorer.py`: `ProfileScorer(base_scorer, profile)` wraps an existing `Scorer`: adds an `AlertHit(family="USER")` for every matching avoid-SMARTS, lowers `composite` accordingly, and applies the profile objectives. Pure wrapper, no engine edits. `profile_id` on `RunConfig` is the field that selects it; document how the server should resolve it.
5. `studio/web/js/account/account.js`: a small, polished UI in the existing dark theme: "Sign in" button in the top bar -> modal (sign up / log in), the username with a menu when logged in, a "My library" drawer listing saved runs and manual sessions with Replay (dispatch `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("metis:replay", {detail: {events}}))` and also call `window.MetisStudio.replayEvents(events)` if it exists), a "Save this run" button that appears on the `run_end` event (subscribe to the bus described in `studio/web/README.md`), and a profile editor (name, objective weight sliders for qed/logp/tpsa/alerts, avoid-SMARTS list with live validation against the server). Works with no backend (hides itself and shows nothing broken).
6. Tests: signup/login happy path, wrong password, duplicate username, rate limit, tampered/expired JWT, CSRF header missing, cross-user isolation on runs/manual/profiles, size caps, SQL-injection-style inputs, SMARTS validation, persistence across app restart (same DB file), JWT secret persistence. Use a test app that composes `studio.server.app.create_app()` (mock mode) + `install(app)`.
Acceptance: tests green; `python -c "from studio.accounts.install import install"` works; a screenshot of the sign-in modal and library drawer (headless browser or in-app browser) in your handoff; document the two wiring lines the integrator must add.
